And the chief of the public security station, to whom I was responsible together with Mladen, was informed by me, had been informed by me, and he told me that he had informed by telephone a superior instance at the republican SUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we could turn your attention to the first of the two visits that you describe in your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, the visits by Radovan Karadzic. That's found in paragraphs 17 through 19. First of all, Mr. Alajbegovic, could you tell us the approximate time, the date when that visit occurred?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The first visit by Mr. Karadzic was in December 1991, at the primary school in Rogatica. Elementary school. It was the Gracanica settlement. That's where the SDS had organised a meeting which was attended by Mr. Karadzic with his escorts. They stayed there for an hour, maybe an hour and a half at the meeting, and I managed to contact Rajko Kusic with respect to providing security for their stay. He refused, and he said that we didn't -- needn't meddle as Muslims in this area, that they would take it upon themselves as Serbs. They would provide security for Karadzic as Serbs, for Karadzic and his men, his people. And after the meeting, we were not able to -- we weren't able to be present in the elementary school building. But after the meeting, they went off to the church for a brief period of time, and the church had already become a -- well, a monastery in 1991. And then they went off together with Mladen Vasiljevic to the Borike area and to the facility there which belonged to the former Prime Minister of Yugoslavia, Mr. Dzemal Bijedic, and Rajko Kusic had already set up his staff there, his headquarters in that building.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, did you personally see Radovan Karadzic during this visit?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I was 20 metres away from him on the plateau in front of the school building, from the time he came out of the vehicle to the time he left the school after the meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what SDS local figures was he with, if any, when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I know that he was greeted in front of the school by Rajko Kusic, who welcomed him. Now, who was inside, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Finally, in respect of the village that they went to after they were in Rogatica, Borike, can you use the pointer and, on Prosecution Exhibit 567, point out the location of Borike, please.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: [Indicates]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Rogatica, Seljani, Satorovici, and Borike.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in your evidence you said that Rajko Kusic had set up a headquarters in Borike. How did you know that and when did he set up that headquarters?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: As early on as January 1991, Rajko Kusic started to establish paramilitary units from supporters of the SDS and by bringing in people from outside, which means bringing in people from Serbia. Paramilitary formations. And then when he had set up the unit, for a time he went underground among Serb villages, and then the whole thing became known, that Rajko Kusic had established that armed formation and that that locality was best suited to him and that he was there with those men fairly frequently, with the units there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me then turn to two issues, please, in your evidence, your written evidence. The elementary school that Radovan Karadzic visited when he came to Rogatica, can you inform the Court what that became after the war started?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did that particular elementary school become, and can you tell the --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The school became a centre, a classical camp from which people were -- which people were brought to and then taken on to secondary school and the nursery in the Rogatica area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what do you base that --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Surrendering point in fact.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On what facts do you base that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: On facts, because I had confirmation from people who did not wish to surrender and who managed to go into hiding and then to leave the area during the night --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: -- under cover of darkness.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have any conversations with any people who did surrender, and did they inform you about this particular elementary school?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Not personally. I didn't talk to the individuals personally, those who surrendered, but I do know from the people who stayed, and as I said previously, those who were eyewitnesses when the Muslim people went to this detention centre from the settlement, and later on they managed to go over to free territory, which was later controlled by the TO units of the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who had command over that detention centre?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Everything was under the control of Rajko Kusic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you know that to be the case?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I know because the people claimed that Rajko, in a vehicle, used a megaphone to make them surrender. He called for their surrender publicly, using a loudspeaker. And then they were moved to the secondary school centre and the detention facility actually there, and then they were transferred to a camp in Rasavnik [phoen], in the Rogatica area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any other facts on which to base your statement that Rajko Kusic had command of this facility? If you do, will you explain those facts to the Judges.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Nothing special, because I wasn't there myself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let us turn, then, to the next area I'd like to direct your attention and that is the second visit of Radovan Karadzic to the Rogatica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: And that, Your Honours, is in paragraph 20 of the statement to the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell -- this visit occurred in approximately March of 1992. How were you aware of this second visit of Radovan Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Right. One of our police officers from Lesna Borike, his name was Camil Arnautovic, and he is dead, unfortunately, he informed me that Radovan Karadzic, that his entourage had arrived. He didn't tell me who the people were in his entourage, he said there was Milivojic [phoen] and commander of the barracks in Han Pijesak, Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Milosevic is Colonel Dragomir Milosevic; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know what position in the army of the Republika Srpska Colonel Dragomir Milosevic later assumed?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know. He was commander of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you describe to the Trial Chamber what occurred after this meeting with Mr. Karadzic and others.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: A couple of days later, the situation aggravated in the entire municipality of Rogatica, meaning that Serb military and paramilitary formations closed off all communications, blocked all roads to prevent communication with Muslim villages and with the legal authorities who were still in Rogatica. Dragan --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- probably came to remove two roadblocks on that road, and I was personally there when he tried, when Rajko Kusic appeared with his men and placed them on both sides of the road. They spoke behind the barricades for a long time, about 40 minutes. Dragomir Milosevic's assistant commander was also there. His name was Asim Dzambasovic, and he was an active-duty officer. When these people arrived, one of the armed men at the roadblock fired two shots in the air to intimidate us, whereas Rajko Kusic spoke to Asim Dzambasovic in these words: "What are you looking for here? This is not your army. Go back to your village Kovanj and line up your troops." In response to that, two officers of the JNA who were there accompanying them tried to calm everybody down to prevent an incident. Forty minutes later the roadblock was removed, however, one still could not go towards the regional road, towards Zepa.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Alajbegovic, you mentioned someone who tried to remove the roadblocks, by the name of Dragan, and then the interpreters could not catch his family name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Dragan meaning Dragomir Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me focus first of all on the unit that you describe as Kusic's paramilitary formations. First of all, how do you know that the units that were at that location were indeed under the command of Rajko Kusic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: We knew that. We knew that because during those negotiations, Rajko displayed in every way that he was in command, and he set conditions and threatened that the worst could occur if we don't agree to the division of territory, surrender, and if the police and the military do not pledge loyalty to the SDS. On one occasion, he even staged an attack in early morning hours in the fields and meadows before Agarovici village, Stara Gora, Stavanj.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, let me interrupt you for a moment. We're focusing on the barricades that you were describing and you said that paramilitary formations appeared. My question is how do you know that those paramilitary formations were Rajko Kusic's paramilitary formations?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: They had special equipment. They wore special camouflage uniforms which was something quite new in our area, never seen before. They had state of the arms -- state-of-the-art weapons, M84 automatic rifles, hand-held rocket launchers, grenades, and they looked like a real military formation, wearing the tricoloured emblems and berets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that Colonel Dragomir Milosevic was also present at the barricades. Can you inform the Trial Chamber what the relationship was between Colonel Dragomir Milosevic and the formations that were under the command of Rajko Kusic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I can. As we were approaching the roadblocks, the barricades, one of the armed men from that military formation fired a shot and said, "Dragomir is the only one who can go forward. Radomir [as interpreted] Milosevic is the only one who can go forward. The rest of you wait back." And that's what happened. Radomir Milosevic went forward. Rajko Kusic went halfway to meet him. They stopped to talk behind the roadblock, and after they emerged we realised that Rajko Kusic, too, is under the command of Radomir Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say he was under the command of Milosevic, what are the facts that support that particular conclusion?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: There are several facts that support that conclusion. Dragomir kept insisting in those negotiations on division of territory. He kept trying to install a complete blockade. With the arrival of these formations, they managed to install a blockade on the entire centre of the town and to prevent civilian authorities from reaching the centre of the town as well as communication with the outside, and Rajko went along with it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say in your evidence that Dragomir kept insisting in those negotiations on the division of territory, what do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the first stage of this division of territory, it was Rogatica that was being divided into the Serb and the Bosniak part. Then the police force was to be divided, followed by the division of territory between two parts of the police force, which part of the territory was supposed to be patrolled by Serb police and Serb paramilitary formations and which by the Bosnian police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: We were not allowed to go into their part of the territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come to that, those sets of negotiations a little bit later, but we're still talking about the roadblock that you've described. Was there anything that particular day that led you to a conclusion that Rajko Kusic was under the command of Colonel Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, we had that impression, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it that day that gave you that impression?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: At that moment, he complied with the order of Colonel Milosevic to remove the roadblock in front of the local commune of Seljani, which means that he was under his orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if -- I would like to direct your attention still to Rajko Kusic's paramilitary formations. Approximately how many men, to your knowledge, were in that paramilitary formation?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: In that well-equipped paramilitary unit that was armed with the most modern equipment, there were between 45 and 50 able-bodied men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in paragraph 26, you indicate that those units were in certain villages. What's the factual basis for that assertion in paragraph 26?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Right. From time to time, he moved across certain local communes of Borike area. Occasionally there were volleys of automatic fire. Rockets were fired and mortar grenades, 82-millimetre calibre, and fire was opened to warn Serb villages that they would be attacked by Muslim forces from Visegrad. And the next day, he asked me at the police station, he said in fact that he could not tolerate that any longer, that he was attacked by Muslim forces from Visegrad, to which I replied that if that was correct, then a multi-ethnic team should be formed using men from Rogatica or from the republican Secretariat of the Interior, because we had estimated based on the material evidence he had brought that machine guns were involved and mortars of a certain calibre, that this assertion was not possible because they -- the police and the others did not have such weapons simply.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is very simple. It's this: How were you aware that Kusic had paramilitary soldiers in the villages of Seljani, Mesici, Pesurici? How were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: We had information that he was moving around that area, that weapons were being fired, and that he was trying to confront Muslim and Serb villages. And then he would move to another area and put in place the same scenario. On one occasion, I went out of Rogatica to a place called Karanfil Mahala --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me stop you, Mr. Alajbegovic. Perhaps you do not fully understand. Mr. Harmon is seeking exactly to establish how did you know. What you do is you say we had information about it and then you describe what the information was. What Mr. Harmon would like to know is how you got that information. Did you see it yourself? Was it reported to you? Did you hear it from other people when you came home in the evening? That's what the question is about.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My answer is very clear: I had information from the ground, and on several occasions I contacted Rajko Kusic personally, as well as his paramilitary units of the SDS, as we called them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you say, "I had information from the ground," was that by your subordinates? Was that by ordinary civilians? Was that by Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. -- what information did you receive, from whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both from my subordinates and from civilians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, proceed, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Kusic was somebody you earlier said you knew. You knew him through negotiations as well as knew him personally; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in -- at some point in time before the conflict started, did Mr. Kusic inform you whose territory Rogatica municipality was?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is preferred if we don't lead on this sort of thing. I would ask Mr. Harmon to reformulate his question, through Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, invitation is to reformulate unless you have major objections of doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have no objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have conversations with Rajko Kusic where he made assertions as to the territory of Rogatica? You have to answer the question aloud.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I can answer very specifically. From September 1991 until the beginning of 1992, Rajko Kusic called me up two or three times, offering me maps and telling me that this was Serbian territory. He produced coloured maps which I received as preposterous, but on the second and third time he was more insistent and even tried to intimidate me, saying that if we insist on seceding from Yugoslavia, we would be deported and expelled unless we pledged loyalty to Serbs because they considered Rogatica to be part of Serb territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he inform you of the basis for his conclusion, why he concluded Rogatica to be Serb territory?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. He tried to explain when we talked that Serbs have more lands registered in their name in land cadastres, or registers, and therefore it was Serbian territory.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, can I direct your attention to paragraph 29, to a conversation that you had with Mr. Kusic in late 1991 during a police SDS meeting at which you attribute a statement to Mr. Kusic "... that there would be no future for Muslims in the area, that we would be attacked if we did not leave." Can you explain to the Judges the circumstances under which that particular statement was made?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: In our eyes, when we later analysed his statement, because I reported it to my superior, it was something like a trial balloon. Rajko Kusic was just testing how we would react to such a sharply formulated condition, namely that we had to leave the area because it was Serb land. That was our conclusion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he raised -- when he made that particular comment to you, were you surprised?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: By that time, I understood it was very serious, and that's why I reported it to my superior.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you said in your answer that there was an analysis of that particular statement. Who conducted that analysis, do you recall?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: It was a briefing between me and the head of the police station in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what conclusion did you reach during that briefing as to the meaning and the import of Rajko Kusic's statement?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I thought I understood what it was all about: Unless we agreed to divide up the territory as they wanted, we could be attacked and the entire Bosniak population could be deported, expelled, or ethnically cleansed, all those who failed to pledge loyalty to the new authorities. However, we continued negotiating because we saw no other way out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you, insofar as the period of late 1991 and early 1992, can you explain to the Judges what pressures were exerted by both Rajko Kusic's paramilitaries and paramilitary formations that you describe in paragraph 27 of your statement, the White Eagles? What kinds of pressures did they exert on the Muslim population?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: By their conduct, by their constant transfers from one place to another, they kept complicating the situation by intimidating the Muslim population. In the course of negotiations, they asked that the legal authorities and police be disarmed. They wanted the police force to be divided, followed by lands, followed by disarmament and surrender. And later, they appealed to people to turn in their weapons, pledge their loyalty to Serb authorities, and hand over all the power to them. And that later proved to be true through our negotiations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Hanoteau would like to put a question to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like you to tell me exactly what was your role, what was your rank within the police at the time. I seem to remember that you were the commander of the local police. That's what I understood. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but there is something called the order of the republican SUP concerning action to be put in place in extraordinary circumstances. It was the order from the republican level dated the 19th September, 1991, which increased the level of mobilisation of the entire police force. Then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question is as follows: You were the commander of the police. How many men did you have under you? How many men did report to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While those joint forces still existed, we had a total of 210 men in the police force, Mladen and I together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But who was your superior in the chain of command, and who were your superiors when it was not in Rogatica? Outside of Rogatica, what was the level, the administrative level above you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The republican Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina; that is, the minister.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you tell us what you witnessed, these events, we gained the impression that you were alone. Did you have the opportunity following the events you describe and that were so serious, did you have the opportunity to take the initiative to report what you were witnessing? Did you draw up reports? Did you go to the administrative centre to -- at the highest level in order to report what you were seeing on the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So what did you do? What did you do, practically speaking?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We sent official reports through dispatches to the republican Secretariat of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina about the establishment of these paramilitary formations headed by Rajko Kusic, about the arrival of paramilitary units from Serbia, the White Eagles wearing their special insignia. Then on the 3rd or 4th March, about the establishment of the Guca Battalion made up of Serb people from Rogatica, among others, who immediately went to the Sarajevo battlefield to fight. That's what you can find in my reports.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are documents you drafted yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I received information and as I went out into the field where I saw many things with my own eyes, I would return to the police station, draft my text and then send it by teleprinter or teletype to the central base of the SUP, the Secretariat of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where was this headquarter of the SUP?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Was there any reaction, any response to your reports, to your telexes? Was there a response?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sometimes we would receive feedback in writing instructing us what to do, what to say in the negotiations so as not to complicate matters further, saying that every effort should be made to avoid conflict and war, if at all possible, whereas some information was given us directly by telephone when they called up the chief of the public security station, who was my superior and the superior of Mr. Vasiljevic as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HANOTEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: One brief question on the paramilitaries and the Uniform Police. Can you describe the differences in the quality of the armament that was possessed by both the paramilitary formations of Rajko Kusic, the types of armament, and the types of armament available to the Uniform Police.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Before that I explained what kind of weapons the paramilitary unit of Rajko Kusic had. If you want me to, I can repeat, and it was this: Automatic weapons, machine-guns of the latest type produced by the JNA, 84 millimetres, hand-held rocket launchers, grenades, special uniforms, and berets with the tricolour emblem, whereas the legal formations, the police force, had the standard type of winter woolen uniforms with windbreakers, wind jackets, and rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What kind of arms were available to the Uniform Police? You said standard rifles. Was there anything else in addition to standard rifles available to the Uniform Police?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: No. We didn't have enough to go around.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention now to paragraph 30 of your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, in which you describe in January of 1992 Rajko Kusic and elements of his paramilitaries opened fire on Serb villages with mortars during the hours of darkness. Can you tell us, first of all, what you know about those particular attacks and how you know that the attacks that you describe in paragraph 30 were committed by Rajko Kusic's paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: We knew about it because he turned up with Mladen Vasiljevic. He came to the police station, the public security police station in Rogatica to inform us that what was going on in the Borike area would not be tolerated. And he also said that allegedly Serb villages had been under attack with mortars, the M82-millimetre type, and that the crater that resulted from the grenades and the M84 machine-gun bullets. We knew and said and claimed that those kinds of weapons did not belong to the police. The police didn't have that type of weapon, the Muslim forces, as they referred to us already at that time, but that it was a trick on his part for him to launch offensive action. When I offered to make up a joint team from the republican SUP and the local police to establish the situation on the ground and provide material evidence and to send them up for analysis, he refused. He refused my offer. And that was a sign to us that they had feigned this attack in order to instil fear into his own people so that they then should undertake operations to clear up the area, which later proved to be true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he -- to your knowledge, were there Muslim Green Berets operating in the Borike area in January of 1992 as he claimed?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: There were no units like that in that area. They referred to all the legal members of the police force as being Green Berets, which was quite absurd as far as we were concerned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me direct your attention to paragraph 39 and also paragraph 5 of the Bosnian statement. I'm going to be covering the area of the disarming of Muslims in villages. In your -- in paragraph 39, you indicate that Kusic accelerated a division between Muslims and Serbs by issuing ultimatums to Muslim villages. Can you be, first of all, more explicit? Tell us when those ultimatums were issued and what the actual words of those ultimatums were.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. During the negotiation stage in the month of March, April, right up to the first half of May, and later on until the 1st of June, Rajko Kusic, because the terrain was divided up and there was no cooperation or communication with the civilian authorities, Rajko managed to disarm or, rather, the -- take away the weapons that were legally in possession of Muslims in certain villages, such as Osovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you identify the villages, could you turn to the Prosecution Exhibit that is next to you, the map 567, and can you point to the villages that you're going to testifying about.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The village of Osovo; Okruglo, Satorovici, the village of Babljak, the village of Burati. Here it is here, Burati. Then ultimatums reached the Kozici local commune for all the Muslim villages. And later on, of course, during the negotiations the ultimatum also applied to the urban area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, how do you know that ultimatums by Rajko Kusic were given to those outlying villages? Were you present when those ultimatums were given to the inhabitants of those villages or was it reported to you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I wasn't present, but people, commissioners, those people who contacted us at the police station would inform us and tell us, would come in or call in and say they had received those orders from these paramilitaries and from him personally, because he took part in all this himself personally. Ah, the village of Strmac. I omitted the village of Strmac a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What specifically was the ultimatum that was reported to you?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The people who informed us from the areas we couldn't reach said that Rajko Kusic had given them an ultimatum by the next day, 12.00 noon or 1300 hours, that all weapons whether in legal possession or not in legal possession should be brought in, and I'm quoting the example of the village of Strmac, that they should be taken to the centre at Strmac, and that's what people did. In the village of Okruglo and Osovo, for example, it was handed over to the school building in Osovo. In Babljak they handed them over to a local commissioner by the name of Goran Marjanovic, for example. Then in the village of Burati they also handed over their weapons and they carried on living there for a certain time but later on they were brought into the holding centres, the collection centres and then the camps, and some were liquidated and no trace of them is known. Their burial place isn't known either. The ultimatums in the Kozici local commune came in, too, and a date was set when the weapons were to be surrendered. However, Rajko Kusic and his formations did not appear in the area, did not go to that locality, but the next day what happened was that they shelled the area, the area was shelled. Pokrivenik, the village of Pokrivenik and they were shelled with 60-millimetre mortars and the 82-millimetre mortars as well. Rocket launchers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the reports that you were receiving from Muslims from these villages about these ultimatums, did you receive information as to what would happen if the weapons were not turned in and what would happen if the weapons were turned in?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell the Judges what you heard.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Rajko's ultimatums said the following: If the weapons were turned in, the people would be guaranteed safety and security and survival, which means that they had demonstrated loyalty to the Serb authorities by turning their weapons in, or rather, to the Serbian Democratic Party, which was in power at the time. All those who failed to turn in their weapons would be expelled, arrested, or suffer the worst consequences.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Rajko Kusic ever make similar demands to you personally?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He kept making them during the negotiations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's turn to these negotiations that you've referred to, Mr. Alajbegovic. Between March of 1992 and May of 1992, were there negotiations between the Muslim representatives and representatives of the SDS in respect of the fate of the territory of the municipality of Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, on several occasions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you participate in those negotiations on behalf of the Muslim authorities?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but not at all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was representing the SDS in those negotiations that took place between March and May of 1992, by name?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Right. Well, in the negotiations on the SDS side, on the Serb people, the main negotiator was Rajko Kusic; Sveto Veselinovic, president of the SDS; Mile Sokolovic. He was later president of the Crisis Staff. That's how they referred to him. Veljko Bojovic. On two occasions Petar Jesic [phoen], Radomir Bukvar [phoen], Mile Ujic as president of the executive authorities of the Rogatica municipality; and on two occasions Novak Dzidan and Mladen Vasiljevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to focus on just the negotiations that took place in March of 1992. Did the SDS put forward proposals to the Muslim representatives in the Rogatica municipality in those negotiations?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the proposals that were put forth by the Serb negotiators in those meetings?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The first proposal was that the police structures should be divided up and that all property should be divided up percentage-wise, depending on what belonged to the Serbian Democratic Party and their representatives in the police force. Then the next one was that there should be a delineation and separation of territory, both for the town of Rogatica and the overall area of the municipality into a Serb portion where Muslim police forces would not be allowed to enter, and if they entered, they -- their security could not be guaranteed. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the police divide in March of 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever have any conversations with your Serb police colleagues as to why this division of the police was occurring?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. There were some of our colleagues from the -- who were Serbs who condemned it. They were the active-duty policemen, my colleagues, in fact, who did not believe in that, pursuing that kind of policy. And then there were the others. There were those whom -- who at that time we qualified and referred to as people from the reserve force which the SDS had brought into the police, and they were extremist in orientation, and they wanted that to take place. They said to us that it was impossible to work together any more, that there was no co-existence any more, that the Serbs were getting their own municipality, republic, and so on and so forth, and they would join up with the Yugoslav People's Army who would be on their side. And if we were to offer resistance, we didn't have a chance, that we would be expelled and so on. Because allegedly, according to them, that was the position taken by the Main Board of the SDS of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you were informed of that directly by members of the Serbian police force in Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me turn to negotiations -- I take it negotiations did continue into April and May, and I'd like to focus your attention on the negotiations in April. In April, you were aware that the war had started in Bosnia; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that there had been --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- already actions in Sarajevo, Bijeljina, Foca, and Visegrad; correct?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, what were the demands of the Serbian negotiators in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: A division of territory, a cartographic, a map division on the map into a Serbia area and a Muslim area, offering -- an offering of maps, and that the SDS should -- that all power should be given over to the SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in respect of the division of the territory, what was the position of the Muslim negotiators in April in respect of the division of the territory?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The Muslim negotiators accepted this division into a Serb Rogatica municipality, and later on they did not want to agree to handing over their power to the SDS or turning in weapons, because we knew the scenario that had been prepared.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why did the Muslim negotiators agree to a division of the territory given that the majority population of the Rogatica municipality was Muslim?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The Muslims went to negotiate to avoid war. They weren't ready for war, regardless of the fact that we were the majority population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the Muslim negotiation position in respect of the SDS demand that full authority of the entire municipality be turned over to them?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The Muslim negotiators tried to put it off, said that they would consult higher instances at state level and that we would receive instructions from them, and if they ordered us to go ahead, then we would follow their orders. It was just to gain time to prevent an attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did those negotiations continue into the month of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to focus your attention on the negotiation session that took place somewhere between the 1st and 5th of May, 1992. Did you personally participate in that negotiation session with representatives of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I was present together with the representatives of the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who from the Serb side was present during those negotiations? Just identify them by name, please.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The meeting was chaired by Milorad Sokolovic as the elected presiding person for the Crisis Staff. That's how he introduced himself. And he was wearing a camouflage uniform. Then there was Veljko Bojovic, and then Mr. Tomo Batinic, and I think Mile Ujic, president of the Executive Board was there too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Rajko Kusic there?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: No. He would just come in from time to time and leave. He would just see that everything was going ahead and then leave. But he had his formations providing security for the school premises where the meetings were being held.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What demands were made by the Serb negotiators in those -- in that particular negotiation?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: In those negotiations the demand was to hand over full authority to the SDS, that the representatives of the Muslim people should call upon the people to surrender their arms, both those that they were in possession of legally and illegally, that they were believed to have in their possession, and that they have no more time to exert pressure, to have pressure exerted on them from the SDS and the military command at Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, were those demands accompanied by assurances that if the Muslims did indeed turn over their weapons, that they would be able to live in peace in the municipality of Rogatica?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but we didn't actually believe it. The war had already begun in other areas, and we were witness through the media of the events that were taking place, and we realised that the same thing was being prepared for the Rogatica municipality, that we'd suffer the same fate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned the name Tomo Batinic. Who is Tomo Batinic, and what position -- what political party did he belong to and what position did he hold?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Tomo Batinic at that point in time was a member of the SDS board for Rogatica, and he performed the duty of director of the payments -- payment transactions for Rogatica. He was then proclaimed president of the municipality of Rogatica, or mayor, and that is the function he holds today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what position he held in the Bosnian Serb administration in Rogatica post-May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: He was president of the Rogatica municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let me ask you, can you relate to the Judges what -- the specifics of the conversation that you had with Mr. Batinic during those negotiations.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Through the negotiations, since I myself was present when they asked for -- asked to turn over authority to the SDS and for the civilian authorities of the Muslim people should call upon the people to surrender and that they would be guaranteed security, I asked him or, rather, Mr. Batinic a direct question because we knew each other very well. I said, "Mr. Tomo, what does all that mean? What does all this mean?" And his answer was this: He said, "We can't wait any longer because there is enormous pressure being exerted on us by the Main Board of the SDS and the military command and that the SAO of Romanija had already been formed and that this coincided with what I said in my statement, and I state it again, that Rogatica officially belonged to the SAO Romanija and that they couldn't wait any longer because pressure was being brought to bear against them to get the job done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And let me then inquire: Did you ask Mr. Batinic about what he meant by those remarks?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did ask him. I said, "What does all this mean?" And he said it meant that they had to carry out the operations and that this belonged to SAO Romanija, which was -- and that Sokolac would be within the frameworks of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to be turning to two exhibits that will take longer than three minutes to introduce, so if we could take a break at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we will have a break. Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom to start with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, could you give us an indication on how much time you'd still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I would say, Your Honour, 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Twenty-five minutes. That keeps you just within the limits of three hours that you indicated. Then, Ms. Loukas, I take it that will then -- the examination in chief will be concluded before the -- before the end of this morning's session, that you could start to cross-examine the witness, well, let's say somewhere 20 minutes past one?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Yes, certainly, Your Honour, I can commence the cross-examination, but obviously it won't be completed today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of course not. We will adjourn until ten minutes to one on this clock, which now shows again the right hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alajbegovic, we were discussing the negotiations that took place between March and May 1992. During the course of those negotiations, are you aware of the negotiators having to discuss various positions taken by the Muslim side with representatives in Pale?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, that question is entirely leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alajbegovic, can you explain to the Judges whether the people who were negotiating from the Serb side in those negotiations that we have been discussing had autonomy to arrive at their own independent decisions or not?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, again. Not as leading as the first, but still leading. In the circumstances, Your Honour, it is better and I think more appropriate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you rather not having leading questions. I understand that. But isn't it true that the witness has testified about pressure from the SDS Main Board? Let me just have a look and see whether -- Ms. Loukas, the witness has testified that there was pressure during the negotiations from the Main Board of the SDS. If you look at page 71, second half of the page. So therefore the question gives a follow-up to -- unless you would say that the Main Board of the SDS was not in Pale at that time, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that's -- that's the point. No foundation has been laid for inserting into the question from the Prosecution Pale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And what's the position of the Defence in respect of the location of the SDS Main Board at that period of time?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think that's a matter for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, could you tell us, the Main Board of the SDS, where it was located during these negotiations. What city or village or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The assumption of our negotiators was that they were in Pale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: How did they assume that? Did they tell you or did you -- how did you know that they assumed that it was in Pale?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With every conversation, every dialogue that we had, they always said they would report to the Main Board of the SDS in Pale. Whether they really did so, I don't know, but that's what they said at the negotiations.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, let me have the next two exhibits marked, please. And if we could start, Madam Registrar, by marking the Tanjug newspaper article as the first exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit number P569. And the newspaper article from Glas P570 [Realtime transcript read in error "P270"].

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you informed, Mr. Alajbegovic, that people from the SDS Rogatica hierarchy travelled to Pale?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was based on what exactly? What was the basis of that information?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The basis of that information was the feedback they presented at that next meeting, namely that they had contacted the Main Board at Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, the two exhibits that I've distributed, one -- we'll start with Prosecution Exhibit 569. Prosecution 569 is a report from the Belgrade Tanjug domestic service that was issued on the 17th of May, and the article refers to in the first paragraph -- and I'll just read relevant portions of the first paragraph into the record. It's dated the 17th of May: "In Sokolac today a meeting was held between representatives of the government of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, the Serb Autonomous Region of Romanija, the Serb municipalities of Osovo and Rogatica, and representatives of the Belgrade based Associations of the Citizens of Romanija Region. The Serb government was represented by Radovan Karadzic and Momcilo Krajisnik, as well as Colonel-General Ratko Mladic, the commander of the military forces of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." Now, in paragraph 3 there's a quotation from Radovan Karadzic, and Mr. Karadzic is quoted as saying: "We know exactly what we want. We want our state in Bosnia and Herzegovina. ... And if they want to take Bosnia and Herzegovina out of Yugoslavia, we want to take our state out of Bosnia and Herzegovina." And finally, there is a quotation in paragraph 5 of this article attributed to Mr. Krajisnik, and I will read this into the record. "Momcilo Krajisnik, president of the Assembly of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, stressed that the time is ripe for a demarcation of the areas between Croats, Serbs, and Muslims because, as he said, a common state with them is no longer possible. Not because we do not want that but because that is what they want. The Muslim leadership has imposed the war on us, even though the Serbs wanted a political solution of all problems, Momcilo Krajisnik said and informed those present that all Serb patriots will have the same emblem, the Serb tricolour." The next exhibit, Your Honour, 570, is obviously a report of the same meeting. This is issued in the newspaper Glas and was issued on the 19th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon, just for the transcript, where you refer to 570 by mistake, the transcript a few lines earlier mentioned 270 as the number attributed, but it should be 570.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've described, sir, the meeting that took place on -- you participated on -- between the 1st and the 5th of May, 1992. Was there another meeting that was scheduled after that meeting?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attend that meeting?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the Muslim representatives who had participated in the earlier negotiations attend that meeting?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was one of the earlier representatives plus a new one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And very briefly, because I want to conclude your testimony in 20 minutes, can you tell the Court what happened at that final meeting as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. After the return of two negotiators from the Muslim side, the ultimatum was that all the people should surrender or, rather, pledge loyalty to the SDS authorities, that they should turn in all the weapons. Failing that, operations were possible in the territory of Rogatica municipality. Since the civilian authorities had estimated earlier that it would not be a good idea for them to attend these negotiations any longer because it served no purpose, they introduced a new negotiator who didn't belong to any of the parties. And at the point when they were negotiating with the Serb negotiators, the chairman was a colonel or lieutenant colonel from Han Pijesak. He was on the side of the Muslim delegation -- or, rather, he was negotiating with the Muslim side. And then in the middle of the negotiations, Rajko Kusic appeared, thinking that the entire delegation was there. He was very surprised to see that none of the earlier negotiators were in attendance. He tried to explain himself to the man from the army who was there together with president of the Crisis Staff, Mile Sokolovic. He was saying that he came there to check their own security situation, to check that nobody brought in any weapons. The lieutenant colonel, however, told him to get out, and he left the room where the negotiations were being conducted, together with his two companions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, turning your attention to paragraph 41, it refers to the arrival of the Uzice Corps on May the 19th, 1992. Let me go back to that third negotiation session. Could you tell the Court approximately the date of the third negotiation session that you just described? When did Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. the third negotiation -- the second negotiation session in May take place? The one you just described.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The last negotiations were after the 10th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were those last negotiations before the arrival of the Uzice Corps?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, because the president of the Crisis Staff, Milorad Sokolovic, had announced back at earlier rounds that if power and weapons were handed over, he would work to bring in the Uzice Corps as a force who would take control of Rogatica municipality and provide security to the Muslim people in return for their pledge of loyalty. And already on the 19th of May, they came in from the site of Rogatica to Kukavice region, and they started disarming the population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say they started disarming the population, what population were they disarming?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The Muslim population that we're talking about, Kukavice village. Civilians who had --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can I --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: -- legal permissions to own hunting rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have approximately 15 minutes to conclude your examination, so listen very carefully to the questions I ask and we will conclude this in the time allotted. Can you first of all tell me the size of the corps, the Uzice Corps, that came into the municipality? What was the size of the units?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't see the corps, because I wasn't in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was reported to you in respect of the size of the units that came in from Uzice Corps?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The commander of the reserve police who was there in the village with 30 of his men, this village being populated by Muslims, told me that they had already taken control of the left and right bank of the river that goes through Kukavice village and that they had already started disarming civilians.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 42 of your evidence, written evidence, you say that on the 22nd of May at 1200 hours, the artillery bombardment started. Is the 22nd of May, 1992, a date that -- to which you attach significance?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That day marked an all-out attack on the town and all the villages that belonged to Rogatica municipality that were populated mainly by Muslims.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As a result of those attacks that commenced on the 22nd of May, can you describe what happened to the villages -- first of all, which villages were attacked, and what happened to the residents of those villages? And you can use, if you would, the exhibit that is beside you on the ELMO. Can you point to the villages?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Just in relation to that question, Your Honour, I think it would be also useful for Mr. Harmon to direct the witness to whether or not he is relating direct knowledge or hearsay, be it first or secondhand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if you could please inform us whether what you have seen by yourself, what you observed by yourself, what you heard, and if you heard it from others by what means and who the others were. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. Members of the reserve police force who were in the Muslim villages at the time used various means of communications to call me at my number to say that the shelling of Muslim villages had started at 1200 hours. I myself was at that point in Kozici local commune, not far from the local branch office, and I spent several hours there in a shelter waiting for the fire from artillery weapons, mortars, machine-guns to end.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which villages were reported to you were under attack?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: It was the entire territory of Zepa municipality. It was populated 90, 90 per cent by Muslims. So the attack was on the entire local commune, the entire town, because the representatives of local authorities were in Bijeljina Polje facing Pasic Kula, Starcici, Kugatici [phoen], Radic, Brda and many other places were shelled at the same time over those three hours. The area of Rasolica [phoen] village, Golubovici, Ferizovici, Vragolovi, Kovanj, while Kosove, Strmac, Burati, Babljak, Demurni [phoen] Don and Mali Zazok [phoen], places that had already turned in their weapons, were spared. This information was later confirmed when people crossed over to the territory where the Territorial Defence had been established from the men coming from these majority Muslim villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When the witness talked about the town, he was pointing at Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, as a result of the events after the artillery attacks started, what happened to the Muslim people who lived in, for example, the town of Rogatica? What did they do?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Many started moving to the secondary school centre and to the Gracanica school to surrender. There were other people who didn't want to do that, and a bit later a clash occurred with Muslim forces in the town itself.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "Muslim forces," very quickly can you tell the Court what you mean by Muslim forces in the city itself.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I mean those Muslims who did not turn in their weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Now, if we could have the next exhibit, please, distributed, presented to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit P571.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, have you seen this exhibit prior to coming into court today?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. What does this exhibit represent?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: This is the list of civilian casualties in the attack on Rogatica mounted by Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I won't go into great detail, but did you -- having reviewed this list, did you know any of these people on this list personally?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, before there are any further questions on this document, if -- I submit it would be important to find out who prepared this document. It seems from the evidence that's been elicited thus far that the witness saw it for the first time when the Prosecution showed it to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes. I showed the witness this document. This came from a Rules of the Road file. It is a list that comprised 20, I think 7 pages. It's a list of people who were killed in various municipalities and I extracted from that list the people who were allegedly killed from Rogatica. This witness has had an opportunity to review this. He has identified -- he knows many of these people and can confirm that. I won't take him through --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you're not asking him to specifically comment on the list but, rather, whether he recognises the names or --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- whether he knows anything about those persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the list is just since it might be difficult to remember all the names. Yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, having reviewed this list, can you confirm that there are people in this list who you know personally and who you can confirm were killed?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let me direct your attention to another topic and that is an exhumation that took place in Duljevac in 1998. Did you attend an exhumation at that location?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges very, very briefly about that mass grave. Just inform the Judges about the detail of that exhumation itself.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Right. We received official information about four Muslim survivors who had surrendered and pledged loyalty to Serb authorities in the months of May and June. Sometime in the first half of July 1992, those people from camps were brought by buses to Kozici local commune in the area of Duljevac village. There were 28 of them. All the 28 of them were placed by Rajko Kusic and his paramilitary forces to act as human shield.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you're now telling us about persons that -- whereas the question was about exhumations. So later if there's any information needed on those bodies exhumated, then Mr. Harmon will certainly ask you. But could you first concentrate, for example, do you know about the exhumation? When did it take place?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The exhumation took place in 1998, when I, being in possession of all this information, went out into the field to the spot where, according to statements by survivors, there was a mass grave, together with a person from the international police force, and there was a prisoner, a survivor who had been taken captive in the Gorazde battlefield. Amor Masevic came back following up on that information to the site to perform the exhumation together with two renowned citizens who had turned in to Serb authorities.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter made a mistake here. Could the witness repeat the last bit. The two Muslims were actually in the grave, they did not come to the exhumation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could you please repeat the last part of your answer because the interpreters would like to hear it again so that they can translate it to us. You said you went out to the spot where, according to the statement the survivors -- there was a mass grave, together with a person from the international police force. Could you please repeat your answer on from that point.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We found the location of the mass grave. We recorded it on the video camera to document it, and seven days later an expert team from the Bosnian authorities, together with Mr. Amor and his team, went to the same location indicated by this video footage and found a mass grave containing 24 bodies of Muslims who had been executed. And these bodies were those of men -- of people who had turned in to Serb authorities in May and June 1992 in the area of Rogatica, and some of these men came from Seljani village. After the exhumation and after the identification of bodies, they were reburied in one of Sarajevo cemeteries in the locality known as Bistrik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alajbegovic, did you personally attend the exhumation?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the identities established of the people who were -- of the bodies that were exhumed from that mass grave?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know some or all of those people whose bodies had been exhumed from the mass grave?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I knew over 90 per cent of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you inform the Judges whether those people were civilians or whether they were combatants.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: They were all civilians who had surrendered to the Serb authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know the professions of some of those people whose bodies were exhumed?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were they?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: There were two doctors, several directors or managers in the commercial organisations from Rogatica, there was a certain number of minors, under age people, and some elderly villagers who had surrendered from the village of the local commune Seljani and others, other places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we can turn your attention -- I can turn your attention to paragraph 47 of the statement given to the Office of the Prosecutor, in that paragraph you describe a letter that was received, and I don't want to go into the details of what is quoted in this particular letter that is represented in the statement. Are there parts of the letter that are not included in paragraph 47, that have not been quoted?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Judges what else this letter contained.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: I personally received a letter in my own hands, a letter from an under-aged boy from the village of Starcici who had been captured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was what was more in the letter which is not quoted here. I would like to ask you to very much focus on it, because the other information we have read, the statement, so therefore we are aware of that. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. The letter, the next portion says the Muslim population. So "population," the word "population" there is missing. And the signature is the SDS of Rogatica permissions office. That is what is missing here in this letter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any additional substance in the letter that is not contained in what is reproduced in paragraph 47?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The details are similar to the letter, and you can find the letter. It was in the intelligence organ at Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Was any reference made to Muslims in this letter that you don't see in the paragraph reproduced?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. The prospects for the Muslim population in Central Bosnia from Visoko to Zenica, that's the portion that's missing. It says "Your perspective of life," as it reads here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any offer in the letter that was made in addition to what's contained in this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The offer was -- that's right, yes. The offer was quite clear that by the 15th of August, we should send a woman, and they would guarantee her safety and security, that she would return, for the forthcoming operation of the cleansing of the terrain and that they would ensure buses to transport the civilians, and in that way they would cleanse the area of the Muslim forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we could turn to the next exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Prosecution Exhibit P572.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, did I ask you to prepare Prosecution Exhibit 572 to reflect the location of the Muslim communities and the Serb communities at the end in December of 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you identify on Prosecution Exhibit 572 where the Muslim population was concentrated in December of 1992.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can. It's marked on this map here. This is the area that comprises the local commune or, rather, the Zepa municipality --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for the record --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: -- which had already been --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For the record, the witness has pointed with the pointer to the area circled in green at the top of the map. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: And then the area of the Muslim villages belonging to the Kozici local commune.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for the record, the witness is using his pointer and indicating the area at the bottom right of the map that is encircled in green.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: And part of the territory of the village of Vrazalice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And for the record, the witness is using his pointer to indicate the area circled in green at the left bottom of the map. Now, in the areas -- in the area that is in between the areas in green, were there any Muslims residing at the end of the December of 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: In green, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many Muslims were residing in the areas that are not circled in green in the Rogatica municipality?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just in relation to that, again a delineation as to whether or not we're talking about direct knowledge --

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I'll get there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, if you would expect the witness to have counted them all, then let's just proceed first and see whether we can start with the cross-examination soon. Please proceed, Mr. Harmon. Of course, the next question would be what would be the basis of his knowledge. No one expects a witness going through the villages, counting all the remaining Muslims. It's really an objection or a suggestion which interrupts rather than assists. Please proceed --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, just in relation to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would now give --

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Just in relation to that, Your Honour, that was not my suggestion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, it was not your suggestion, but you should not have interfered and you should have let Mr. Harmon go at this moment in time. Please proceed, Mr. Harmon.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm performing my duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Harmon. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you've indicated three areas where the Muslims were concentrated in December of 1992. The other areas that are not circled in green, what was the majority ethnic group that resided in that area?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: At that point in time, most of them were Muslims. They were all brought to the camps, which means that they had been cleansed ethnically.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask the question again, okay, and I'd like you to listen to the question very carefully. You have a map, 572, that is on the ELMO in front of you. I asked you a question to identify three areas, the areas where the Muslim population was concentrated in December of 1992, and you pointed out three areas that are circled in green. The rest, the remaining part of the Rogatica municipality is not circled in green. What was the majority ethnic population that resided in the area of Rogatica municipality that is not circled in green?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: In 1992, December; is that right?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: December of 1992; correct.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The Serb population.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is, to your knowledge, how many Muslims remained in the area that is not circled in green in the Rogatica municipality in December of 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The couple of villages that we mentioned earlier on, but they were all brought to the camps in Rogatica, which means that they weren't in their homes any longer in 1992. They were already in the camp in Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court what happened to the mosques that existed in the Rogatica municipality by the end of December of 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. All the mosques, two city mosques and 30 mosques in the Rogatica municipality in the villages, except the mosque in the village of Lubardici were mined and blasted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you -- did you see that personally or were you informed of that information?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: At the time, I didn't personally see it, but later on we learnt from others, and at the end of the war I visited many of these places and saw for myself that those mosques were no longer standing. And in the town itself on the spot where the mosque stood was a parking lot instead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me direct your attention to paragraph 52 of the statement provided -- provided to the Office of the Prosecutor. Can you inform the Trial Chamber the facts upon which you base the information contained in paragraph 52.

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
