utterances.text: Yes. What is meant is the Muslim people who had come to see what was going to happen next in front of those detainee camps in the school. They were arrested there, captured. Many of them were beaten up. Many of them were liquidated or taken off into the night, and to the present day the whereabouts of many is not known. We don't know where they were killed and where the mass graves lie --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Alajbegovic --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: -- in which there are still many --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- did you personally see that or was that information that you received through reports?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Information from reports and the statements of people who in one way or another had reached the authorities of Bosnia-Herzegovina and were able to tell, who had reached the BH army.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you in paragraph -- I'm referring you to paragraph 53. You arrive at a conclusion. Can you tell the Court the factual basis for the conclusion that you include in paragraph 53. What are the facts?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Very simple: That the politics and policies of the SDA from Rogatica followed the official positions and policy taken by the SDS of the Republika Srpska for ethnic cleansing, persecution, and expulsion and the creation of the state of Republika Srpska. And this came to prove true in practice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: Because all the commands, all the orders came from top level down to the lower levels.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, in your evidence, in your answer, you said, and I quote, "That the politician and policies of the SDA..." Is that correct? Let me read your complete answer. "That the policies -- that the politics and policies of the SDA from Rogatica followed the official positions and policy taken by the SDS of the Republika Srpska."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter said SDS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's a small mistake on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me explore this with you a little bit more, Witness. When is the factual basis that -- what are the facts that you have at your disposal showing that the Serbs carried out a well-planned, large-scale operation commanded at the highest level? What are the facts that you base that conclusion on?

utterances.speaker: RAMIZ ALAJBEGOVIC
utterances.text: The facts are that there was combat operations against the territories where the Muslims were concentrated, and the object of that was to expel us from those parts, too, which means that everything had been planned from the highest level and staged right down to the lower commands in order to expulse the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were asked about facts. Your position is clear but if you say what the object was, that's not fact. So if you say, for example, command highest level, how did you know it was the highest level and not another level or no level at all?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes, you could feel it because there were military formations at their disposal. They had heavy weaponry, the aviation and everything that was at their disposal was directed against expelling the Muslims from those areas; the setting up of camps, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just try to understand you. Therefore, you say they had weaponry and aviation and that was not available at any other level than the highest level. Is that a correct understanding of what you want to say? So that's one fact which supports your conclusion. That's the weaponry.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you give us similar facts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Furthermore, the ultimatums expressed in the negotiations to surrender weapons, to be loyal to Serb authorities, failing which we would be deported and ethnically cleansed from those areas proved to be true in other territories. In those three areas along those three axes where Muslim forces were concentrated, operations were later developed, such as the Zepa enclave operation, and these areas were cleansed from the Muslim population. That is another fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You say if I compare from what I know, even if not by your own observation, what happened in Rogatica and what happened in Zepa and by comparing that I draw the conclusion that -- then it should have been organised at the highest levels because of the pattern or consistency?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Harmon, I don't know whether you want to explore that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I don't, Your Honour. I have no additional questions. I conclude my direct examination. Thank you very much, Mr. Alajbegovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, of course I could invite you to start your cross-examination. It doesn't make much sense perhaps for the last three or four minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: There is just one point. Your Honour will recall back on page 89 I made an objection that Your Honour characterised as interfering with Mr. Harmon. I would indicate, Your Honour, I'm sorry if Your Honour gained that impression. I was trying to be helpful because I think it's critical that when the evidence in chief comes out, that the basis of knowledge is made. In any event, Mr. Harmon indicated that he would come to the basis of knowledge, and if one looks back at page 89, actually the basis of knowledge was not come to, and I think prior to finishing the evidence in chief, it would be appropriate that we actually now do finally find out whether the basis of the knowledge was firsthand or secondhand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do agree with you. At the same time, I would have expected Mr. Harmon to -- as a matter of fact, the question put by Mr. Harmon finally was not really answered.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Precisely, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So I fully acknowledge, although I thought at that time that you're not greatly assisting, certainly at this time you do, at this moment you do.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I will be glad to ask the witness that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Alajbegovic, Mr. Harmon had some difficulties in getting an answer to his question how many Muslims remained by the end of 1992, December 1992, in the area not circled green? And then you said they were taken to camps. How many were still there living in their own homes in the non-green encircled areas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was the Burati village.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And there they were still living. Could you please point at the Burati village. Could we perhaps have the map again on the ELMO. Could you point at it. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a village near the thoroughfare from Sarajevo to Rogatica, near a place called Stjenice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I then understand that there Muslims were still living in their own houses at -- in December 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Occasionally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What do you mean by that? Do you mean not all of them, or now and then, or ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I mean is that they were occasionally taken away to give logistical support to the Serb army on the front line and to perform various jobs for the Serbian army in the fields, in the town, anywhere. And in 1995, these people were exchanged.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, apart from the village of Burati, where were still Muslims living in the non-green encircled area and how many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A small number, Osovo and Okruglo villages. These villagers would occasionally be taken to camps. They would be used to dig trenches. Some of them were eventually killed, others survived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any other -- in total, how many Muslims were still living in the non-green encircled area, approximately? I'm not asking an exact number at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Around a hundred.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that's including the villages you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. What makes you say that there were approximately a hundred? On what is this assessment or this number based?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When the exchange took place in 1995 in the Kula prison in what was then the Serbian part of Sarajevo, those people came to the territory of the federation and I was in a position to see them, to conduct interviews with them, and that's how I got the information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could there have been a larger number if not all of them were exchanged so that there were others still remaining?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, nobody stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That means that after the exchange, that there were no Muslims living at all any more in the area not green encircled? How did you know that? I mean, what made it possible for you to verify this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We knew that two families had remained in the town. I don't know what their fate became, but I know they stayed until the end of the war. Whether they were later exchanged or whether they were sent to third countries, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Harmon, I've tried to clarify some of the issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: I have no additional questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You have no further questions. Ms. Loukas, we are past a quarter to two. If there is any very urgent matter, please raise it. If not, you may start to cross-examine the witness tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. Just very quickly, we've organised a conference with Mr. Krajisnik for 6.00 this evening, and the Registry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is the witness to be informed about all this?

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: The witness doesn't need to be here for this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'd like to continue tomorrow morning, 9.00, same courtroom. We would like to see you back. May I instruct you not to speak with anyone about your testimony that you have given until now, nor to speak with anybody about your testimony still to be given tomorrow when you'll be cross-examined by the Defence. Madam Usher, would you please escort Mr. Alajbegovic out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Loukas, you've planned a meeting for 6.00 this evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour, and I can indicate that I have spoken to Ms. Meleras, Michelle Meleras, from the Registry and she's very helpfully trying to organise an interpreter for us this afternoon, and of course, the question of interpreters and conferences with Mr. Krajisnik has become rather difficult in the absence of a case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm aware of that and it's good to hear that at least the Registry does everything to support the Defence in this.

utterances.speaker: MS. LOUKAS
utterances.text: Indeed they do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00, same courtroom, with apologies for the interpreters and the technicians for the additional five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
